'''Barry Smith''' (born 4 June 1952) is an Anglo-American philosopher researching in the field of [[applied ontology]].

==Education==
From 1970 to 1973, Smith studied Mathematics and Philosophy at the [[University of Oxford]]. He obtained his [[PhD]] from the [[Victoria University of Manchester|University of Manchester]] in 1976 for a dissertation on ontology and reference in [[Edmund Husserl|Husserl]] and [[Gottlob Frege|Frege]].<ref name="phd">{{cite thesis|degree=PhD |first=Barry |last=Smith |title=The Ontology of Reference: Studies in Logic and Phenomenology |publisher=University of Manchester |date=1976 |url=https://uomlibrary.access.preservica.com/portal/en-US/asset/sdb:IO%7Cf4108fc8-ed0b-4c57-a5e3-7b0b9927f8ba}}</ref> The dissertation was supervised by [[Wolfe Mays]].

Among the cohort of graduate students supervised by Mays in Manchester at that time were [[Kevin Mulligan]] (Geneva/Lugano), and [[Peter Simons (academic)|Peter Simons]] (Trinity College, Dublin). Both shared with Smith an interest in analytic metaphysics and in the contributions of turn-of-the-century Continental philosophers and logicians to central issues of analytic philosophy.<ref>Mark Textor (ed.), ''The Austrian Contribution to Analytic Philosophy'', Routledge, 2006. {{ISBN|9780415404051}}.</ref><ref>Thomas Uebel, "The Neurath-Haller Thesis and the Return of Analytic Philosophy to Austria", ''Grazer Philosophische Studien'', ''Grazer Philosophische Studien'', 101 (2024) 249–276 {{DOI:10.1163/18756735-00000222}}.</ref> In 1979 they together founded the Seminar for Austro-German Philosophy,<ref>Axel Bühler, "[http://ontology.buffalo.edu/smith/articles/drei_briten.pdf Drei Briten in Kakanien]", ''Information Philosophie'', 3 (1987), 22–33.</ref> which organized workshops and conferences centered around the work of early Central European philosophers from [[Bernard Bolzano|Bolzano]] to [[Alfred Tarski|Tarski]] and their impact on subsequent generations. A central role in this respect was played by Husserl's contributions to formal ontology.<ref>Sébastien Richard, "Object and Something in General in Contemporary Formal Ontology", in Fosca Mariani Zini (ed.), ''The Meaning of Something'', Springer, 2022. 133-149. DOI: 10.1007/978-3-031-09610-5_6.</ref> [[Roderick Chisholm]] refers to the role played by these meetings in contemporary philosophy.<ref>See L. E. Hahn (ed.), ''The Philosophy of Roderick Chisholm'' (Library of Living Philosophers), Chicago and La Salle, IL, 1997, p. 17.</ref>

==Career==
Smith has held academic posts at the [[University of Sheffield]], the [[Victoria University of Manchester|University of Manchester]], the [[:de:Internationale Akademie für Philosophie|International Academy of Philosophy]] ([[Liechtenstein]]), and since 1994 at the [[University at Buffalo, The State University of New York|University at Buffalo]].<ref name="CV">{{Cite web|url=http://ontology.buffalo.edu/smith/BSCV.pdf|title=Barry Smith – CV}}</ref> In 2025 Smith established in collaboration with John Beverley an online [https://dailynous.com/2025/10/30/new-online-masters-program-in-applied-ontology/ Masters and PhD degree programs in Applied Ontology].<ref>Program hub: https://ontology.buffalo.edu</ref> His students in Buffalo have included: [[Berit Brogaard]], Leo Zaibert<ref>Hirsch Professor of Penal Theory and Ethics in the [[University of Cambridge]], {{cite web | url=https://www.crim.cam.ac.uk/people/professor-leo-zaibert | title=Professor Leo Zaibert | date=September 2022 }}</ref>, [https://www.linkedin.com/in/ryan-riccucci-491b211b8/ Ryan Riccucci] and [[John Beverley (ontologist)|John Beverley]]. 

From 2002 to 2006, Smith served as Director of the Institute for Formal Ontology and Medical Information Science (IFOMIS), initially in [[Leipzig]] and then, from 2004, in [[Saarbrücken]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uni-saarland.de/institut/ifomis/history.html|title=History|first=Universität des|last=Saarlandes|website=www.uni-saarland.de}}</ref>

In 2005, Smith founded the National Center for Ontological Research (NCOR), under the auspices of which he initiated in 2006 the Ontology for the Intelligence Community, subsequently STIDS,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://kadsci.com/stids2024/|title=STIDS2024 - KaDSci|date=14 March 2024}}</ref> conference series. In 2009 he founded the International Conference on Biomedical Ontology (ICBO).<ref>Barry Smith, ed., ''Proceedings of the First International Conference on Biomedical Ontology'', Buffalo, New York, July 24–26, 2009. [https://buffalo.box.com/shared/static/1vxdgn0r35auhzrswdy6kf1vscf7o32c.pdf], last accessed August 25, 2017.</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://dblp.org/db/conf/icbo/index.html | title=DBLP: International Conference on Biomedical Ontology }}</ref>

From 1992 to 2016, Smith served as editor of ''[[The Monist |The Monist: An International Quarterly Journal of General Philosophical Inquiry]]''.

From 2016, he served as editor of international standard [[ISO/IEC 21838]]: Top Level Ontologies, Parts 1 and 2, which were published by ISO in 2021. Part 1<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.iso.org/standard/71954.html|title=ISO/IEC 21838-1:2021|website=ISO}}</ref> specifies the requirements for being a top-level (which means: domain-neutral) ontology. Part 2<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.iso.org/standard/74572.html|title=ISO/IEC 21838-2:2021|website=ISO}}</ref> is devoted to [[Basic Formal Ontology]] (BFO). In its issue of September 28, 2022 the ''[[Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung]]'' refers to BFO as the first example of a piece of philosophy that has been accepted as an industrial norm, describing this as a 'small sensation in the history of science'.<ref>{{Cite web | title=Begriffe in Schichten: Die 'Basic Formal Ontology' erbringt Dienstleistungen für die Medizin. Das wurde jetzt mit der Anerkennung als Industriestandard gewürdigt | language=de | trans-title=Terms in layers: The 'Basic Formal Ontology' provides services for medicine. This has now been recognized with its recognition as an industry standard| url=https://buffalo.box.com/v/KI-und-Philosophie}}</ref>

In the course of his career, Smith has held visiting positions at universities in Austria, Finland, Malta, and the Netherlands; as well as in the University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center; in the Ecole des Hautes Etudes en Sciences Sociales, Paris,<ref>{{Cite web| title=Barry Smith - Curriculum Vitae | date=July 29, 2006 | url=http://ontology.buffalo.edu/smith/BSCV.pdf | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060901103209/http://ontology.buffalo.edu/smith/BSCV.pdf | archive-date=2006-09-01}}</ref> and also in the Ricerche di Dinamica dei Sistemi e di Bioingegneria (LADSEB), now the Laboratory for Applied Ontology,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.loa.istc.cnr.it/|title=Laboratory for Applied Ontology (LOA)}}</ref> in Padua.<ref>Nicola Guarino, "BFO and DOLCE: So far, so close ..." (2017), ''Cosmos + Taxis'', 4 (4):10-18 (2017), {{Cite web|title=Bfo and Dolce: So Far, so Close?|work=Cosmos + Taxis|date=2017|volume=4|issue=4|pages=10–18|url=https://philarchive.org/rec/GUABAD|last1=Guarino|first1=Nicola}}.</ref>

Since 2019, Smith has served as visiting professor in the [[University of Italian Switzerland]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=2020|title=Professors|url=https://www.usi.ch/en/education/master/philosophy/professors|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201001010749/https://www.usi.ch/en/education/master/philosophy/professors |archive-date=1 October 2020 |access-date=November 11, 2020|website=usi.ch - Master in Philosophy}}</ref>

==Research activities==

=== Historical background of work in ontology ===

From the beginning of his career, Smith worked in the field of [[ontology]], his interest in this field having been prompted by the book ''Time and Modes of Being''<ref>''Time and Modes of Being'', translated by Helen R. Michejda, Springfield, Illinois: Charles C. Thomas, 1964.</ref> by the Polish philosopher [[Roman Ingarden]]. At first he focused on the history of [[philosophical ontology|ontology as a sub-discipline of philosophy]], focusing especially on philosophers in the tradition of [[Franz Brentano|Brentano]] and [[Edmund Husserl|Husserl]], including not only Ingarden but also other pupils of Husserl such as [[Adolf Reinach]] and [[:de:Johannes Daubert|Johannes Daubert]].<ref>Karl Schuhmann, Barry Smith, "Against Idealism: Johannes Daubert vs. Husserl's ''Ideas'' I", ''The Review of Metaphysics'', 38 (4) (June 1985), 763-793</ref><ref>Marco Tedeschini, From Phenomenology to Formal Ontology: How Barry Smith and Kevin Mulligan Made Husserl’s Descriptive Psychology into a Form of Realism, ''Archivio di filosofia'', 83 (3), 2015, 177-188.</ref><ref>Daniel R. Sobota, "The Question of Reality. A Postscript to Schuhmann and Smith on Daubert’s Response to Husserl’s ''Ideas I''", in Rodney K. B. Parker (ed.), ''The Idealism-Realism Debate Among Edmund Husserl’s Early Followers and Critics'', Cham: Springer Verlag. pp. 135-149 (2021)</ref> A special focus was on the theory of ontological dependence and part-whole relations proposed by Husserl,<ref>Fabrice Correia, "Ontological Dependence", ''Philosophy Compass'' 3/5 (2008): 1013–1032, 10.1111/j.1747-9991.2008.00170.x</ref><ref>Kit Fine, "Part-Whole", ''Cambridge Companion to Husserl'', Cambridge University Press, 1995.</ref> a theory which was applied by Husserl's students for example to the understanding of the ontology of mental and linguistic acts.<ref>Kevin Mulligan, ed., ''Speech Act and Sachverhalt: Reinach and the Foundations of Realist Phenomenology'', Reidel, 1987.</ref> In 1984 he co-authored the paper "Truth-Makers",<ref>Kevin Mulligan, Peter Simons and Barry Smith, Truth-Makers, ''Philosophy and Phenomenological Research'', 44 (1984), 287-321.</ref> which is said to have "introduced the truth-maker idea as a contribution to the correspondence theory of truth",<ref>D. M. Armstrong, ''Truth and Truthmakers'', Cambridge University Press, 2004.</ref><ref>[http://plato.stanford.edu/entries/truthmakers/ Fraser MacBride, "Truthmakers"], ''Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy'' (2013).</ref><ref>[[Philip Larrey]], From Searle’s Speech Acts to Smith’s Truth-Makers, Raffaela Giovagnoli and Robert Lowe (eds.), ''The Logic of Social Practices'', New York: Springer, 2020, 37-48.</ref> a still-active research program at the borderlines of logic, semantics and philosophical ontology that is based on a new understanding of the [[correspondence theory of truth]].

=== Geospatial ontology ===

From the mid-1990s, Smith's work in ontology has exerted an impact on multiple domains outside philosophy,<ref>Thomas Pradeu, Maël Lemoine, Mahdi Khelfaoui, and Yves Gingras (2024). "Philosophy in science: Can philosophers of science permeate through science and produce scientific knowledge?." ''The British Journal for the Philosophy of Science'', 75(2), 375-416.</ref> starting in 1995 in a collaboration with [[David Mark (scientist)|David Mark]], one of the founders of [[geographic information science]] (GIS). In this connection Smith introduced the idea of ''fiat objects''<ref>Barry Smith, "[http://ontology.buffalo.edu/smith//articles/fiatobjects.pdf Fiat Objects]", ''Topoi'', 20: 131–148, 2001.</ref> to describe (often rectangular) geospatial entities, such as postal districts and real estate parcels, which are not separated from their surroundings by any physical discontinuity.<ref>Kim Lowell, "Fiat boundaries: some implications for interpretation, decision-support, and multi-temporal analysis." ''Environmental and ecological statistics'' 15 (2008): 369-383.</ref> This idea has been adopted also in other fields.<ref>Richard Davies (ed.), ''Natural and Artifactual Objects in Contemporary Metaphysics. Exercises in Analytic Ontology'', London: Bloomsbury, 2019.</ref><ref>L. Vogt, P. Grobe, B. Quast, T. Bartolomaeus, "[https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0048603 Fiat or Bona Fide Boundary — A Matter of Granular Perspective"], ''PLoS ONE'', 7(12): e48603.</ref><ref>Faith Sternlieb, ''et al'', [https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2013.08.053 A Question of Fit: Reflections on Boundaries, Organizations and Social–Ecological systems], ''Journal of Environmental Management'', 130, 2013, 117-125.</ref><ref>Evans, M. J., & Stoffle, R. W. (2026). "[https://doi.org/10.3390/land15091587 Where Does a Sacred Place End? Rethinking Boundaries in Heritage Stewardship]", ''Land'', 15(9), 1587.</ref>

=== Biomedical ontology ===

Since 2000, much of Smith's research has been centered on the application of ontology in [[biomedical informatics]], where he has worked on a variety of projects relating to biomedical terminologies and electronic health records.<ref>Martin Berzell, ''Electronic Healthcare Ontologies: Philosophy, the Real World and IT Structures'', Linköping Studies in Arts and Science, 2010, No. 517. [http://liu.diva-portal.org/smash/get/diva2:310618/FULLTEXT01.pdf]</ref> He is a founding coordinating editor of the [[Open Biomedical Ontologies|OBO Foundry]],<ref>Barry Smith, et al., "The OBO Foundry: coordinated evolution of ontologies to support biomedical data integration", ''Nature Biotechnology'' 25, 1251-1255 (2007). {{doi|10.1038/nbt1346}}</ref> and has served as a member of the Scientific Advisory Board of the [[Gene Ontology]] (GO) Consortium and of the [[Ontology for Biomedical Investigations]] (OBI).<ref>Anita Bandrowski, et al., "The Ontology for Biomedical Investigations", ''PLOS One'', April 29, 2016. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0154556</ref> He contributes to the development of a number of biological and biomedical ontologies, including the Protein Ontology,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://proconsortium.org/|title=Protein Ontology|website=proconsortium.org}}</ref> the Plant Ontology,<ref>Ramona Lynn Walls, Laurel Cooper, Justin Lee Elser, Maria Alejandra Gandolfo, Christopher J Mungall, Barry Smith, Dennis William Stevenson, Pankaj Jaiswal, "The Plant Ontology facilitates comparisons of plant development stages across species", ''Frontiers in Plant Science'', June 4, 2019, 10, 631. [https://doi.org./0.3389/fpls.2019.00631]{{Dead link|date=August 2025|bot=InternetArchiveBot|fix-attempted=yes}}</ref> and others. Between 2005 and 2015 he was a co-PI of the NIH [[National Center for Biomedical Ontology]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.buffalo.edu/ubreporter/archive/vol37/vol37n6/articles/OntologyCenter.html|title=UB part of new NIH center - UB Reporter|website=www.buffalo.edu}}</ref> where he was responsible especially for dissemination of ontology best practices and for providing training opportunities for biomedical ontologists.<ref>Chelsea Wald, “More Than Words”, ‘’Science’’, 2011/02, {{doi|10.1126/science.caredit.a1100012}}</ref> Between 2013 and 2018 he served as ontology lead on the [[National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases|NIAID]] ImmPort project.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://immport.org/shared/|title=ImmPort Shared Data|website=immport.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.buffalo.edu/ubnow/stories/2013/smith_nih_immunology.html|title=UB ontologists supporting NIH grant|website=www.buffalo.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bhattacharya |first1=Sanchita |last2=Dunn |first2=Patrick |last3=Thomas |first3=Cristel G. |last4=Smith |first4=Barry |last5=Schaefer |first5=Henry |last6=Chen |first6=Jieming |last7=Hu |first7=Zicheng |last8=Zalocusky |first8=Kelly A. |last9=Shankar |first9=Ravi D. |last10=Shen-Orr |first10=Shai S. |last11=Thomson |first11=Elizabeth |last12=Wiser |first12=Jeffrey |last13=Butte |first13=Atul J. |date=2018 |title=ImmPort, toward repurposing of open access immunological assay data for translational and clinical research |journal=Scientific Data |volume=5 |article-number=180015 |doi=10.1038/sdata.2018.15  |doi-access=free|pmc=5827693 |pmid=29485622|bibcode=2018NatSD...580015B }}</ref>

=== Social ontology ===

Smith works also on the ontology of social reality, particularly in connection with the work of [[John Searle]].<ref>Bauwens M. "Institutions as dispositions: Searle, Smith and the metaphysics of blind chess". ''Journal of the Theory of Social Behavior'' 2018;1–19. https://doi.org/10.1111/jtsb.12161</ref> He served as consultant to [[Hernando de Soto Polar|Hernando de Soto]], director of the [[Institute for Liberty and Democracy]] in Peru, on projects relating to the advancement of property and business rights among the poor in developing countries.<ref>Smith, B. Searle and De Soto: The New Ontology of the Social World. In B. Smith, D. Mark & I. Ehrlich (eds.), ''The Mystery of Capital and the Construction of Social Reality''. Chicago: Open Court. pp. 35-51 (2008)</ref> De Soto's work is based on the crucial role of documents—title deeds, stocks and shares, insurance policies—in ensuring the sorts of rights with which we are accustomed in developed economies. Drawing on De Soto's ideas Smith proposed a theory of document acts that would parallel the theory of speech acts developed by Reinach in 1913 and then by J. L. Austin and Searle in the 1960s.<ref>B. Smith, “[https://philpapers.org/archive/SMIHTD.pdf How to Do Things with Documents]”, ''Rivista di Estetica'', 50 (2012), 179-198.</ref><ref>B. Smith, “[http://ontology.buffalo.edu/smith/articles/document-acts.pdf Document Acts]”, in A. Konzelmann Ziv and H. B. Schmid (eds.), ''Institutions, Emotions, and Group Agents. Contributions to Social Ontology'', Dordrecht: Springer, 2014, 19-31.</ref>

=== Intelligence, defense and security ===

Since 2008, Smith has worked on ontology initiatives in the military and intelligence field. In 2008–2010 he served as technical lead on a project sponsored by the US Army Net-Centric Data Strategy Center of Excellence (ANCDS CoE) to create the [[Universal Core]] Semantic Layer (UCore-SL). Since 2010 he was worked on a series of initiatives sponsored by the US Army [[Intelligence and Information Warfare Directorate]] (I2WD) to create a framework for semantic enhancement of intelligence data in the Cloud. Since 2014 he is collaborator on initiatives of the US [[Air Force Research Laboratory]] on planning, mission assurance, and lifecycle management. In this connection he has worked on the creation of an ontology for joint [[military doctrine]],<ref>Peter Morosoff, Ron Rudnicki, Jason Bryant, Robert Farrell & Barry Smith, "Joint Doctrine Ontology: A Benchmark for Military Information Systems Interoperability", ''Semantic Technology for Intelligence, Defense and Security'' (STIDS), CEUR vol. 1325, 2015, pp. 2-9.</ref> designed to support the use of information technology in joint operations by allowing computational access to the contents of Joint Doctrine publications.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.jcs.mil/Portals/36/Documents/Doctrine/pubs/status.pdf?ver=2019-07-30-091515-693|title=Joint Doctrine Hierarchy}}</ref> He has also contributed to the ecosystem of Space Domain Ontologies created under the direction of CUBRC in Buffalo,<ref>Alexander P. Cox, et al., [https://philpapers.org/archive/COXTSD-2.pdf The Space Domain Ontologies]. In ''National Symposium on Sensor & Data Fusion Committee'' (2021)</ref> and he is one of the founding members of the Department of Defense and Intelligence Community Ontology Working Group (DIOWG), now the National Security Ontology Working Group (NSOWG).

In January 2024, a memorandum was signed by the chief data officers of the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI) and of the DOD Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office (CDAO) establishing BFO as 'baseline standards for ontology development' in the DOD and Intelligence Community.<ref>{{Cite web| title=Baseline Standards for Formal Ontology within the Department of Defense and the Intelligence Community | date=March 2024 | url=https://dailynous.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/memo-dod-applied-ontology.pdf | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240311205124/https://dailynous.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/memo-dod-applied-ontology.pdf | archive-date=2024-03-11}}</ref><ref>Bert Gambini, ''[https://www.buffalo.edu/news/releases/2024/02/department-of-defense-ontology.html DOD, Intelligence Community adopt resource developed by UB ontologists]'', University at Buffalo News Center, 28 February 2024.</ref>

=== Industrial Ontologies Foundry ===

Since 2016, Smith has been involved in the Industrial Ontologies Foundry (IOF) initiative,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://oagi.org/pages/industrial-ontologies|title=Industrial Ontologies|website=OAGi}}</ref> which is creating a set of open ontologies to support the data needs of the manufacturing and engineering industries in a way that will advance data interoperability. [[Basic Formal Ontology]], which serves as the top-level hub of the IOF, has been applied in the development of ontologies in many areas of engineering,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://ncorwiki.buffalo.edu/index.php/BFO-Based_Engineering_Ontologies|title = BFO-Based Engineering Ontologies - NCOR Wiki}}</ref> including maintenance,<ref>Hedi Karray, Farhad Ameri, Melinda Hodkiewicz, Thierry Louge, [https://www.researchgate.net/publication/332390146_ROMAIN_Towards_a_BFO_compliant_reference_ontology_for_industrial_maintenance ROMAIN: Towards a BFO compliant reference ontology for industrial maintenance], ''Applied ontology'', vol. 14, no. 2, 179-197.</ref> supply chain,<ref>Ana Correia, Dragan Stokic, Rebecca Siafaka, Sebastian Scholze, ''[https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/8280014 Ontology for Collaborative Development of Product Service Systems based on Basic Formal Ontology]'', ''2017 International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Innovation (ICE/ITMC)''.</ref> product life cycle,<ref>J. Neil Otte, Dimitris Kiritsis, Munira Binti Mohd Ali, Ruoyu Yang, Binbin Zhang, Ron Rudnicki, Rahul Rai, Barry Smith, [https://philpapers.org/archive/OTTAOA-3.pdf An Ontological Approach to Representing the Product Life Cycle], ''Applied Ontology'', vol. 14, no. 2, 155-177.</ref> and additive manufacturing.<ref>Thomas J. Hagedorn, Sundar Krishnamurty & Ian R. Grosse, [http://computingengineering.asmedigitalcollection.asme.org/article.aspx?articleid=2674329 A Knowledge-Based Method for Innovative Design for Additive Manufacturing Supported by Modular Ontologies], ''Journal of Computing and Information Science in Engineering'', 18(2), 021009 (Mar 19, 2018).</ref>

=== Artificial intelligence and complex systems ===

In 2022, Smith and German scientist Jobst Landgrebe co-authored the book ''Why Machines Will Never Rule the World. Artificial Intelligence Without Fear''.<ref>Jobst Landgrebe and Barry Smith, [https://www.routledge.com/Why-Machines-Will-Never-Rule-the-World-Artificial-Intelligence-without/Landgrebe-Smith/p/book/9781032309934 ''Why Humans Will Never Rule the World. Artificial Intelligence Without Fear''], Abingdon, UK: Routledge, 2022, ISBN 978-1-00-331010-5.</ref><ref>Thomas Jefferson Snodgrass, ''[https://www.snodgrass.blog/why-machines-will-never-rule-the-world/ Why Machines Will Never Rule the World]'', 2024, [https://www.astralcodexten.com/p/book-review-contest-2023-winners?ref=snodgrass.blog Finalist in the Astral Codex Top Ten Book Review Contest].</ref> A symposium on the book was published in the journal ''Cosmos + Taxis''.<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://cosmosandtaxis.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/ct_vol12_iss_5_6_epub.pdf | title=COSMOS + TAXIS - Studies in Emergent Order and Organization | website=cosmosandtaxis.org}}</ref> and a second, revised and enlarged, edition appeared in May 2025.<ref>https://www.routledge.com/Why-Machines-Will-Never-Rule-the-World-Artificial-Intelligence-without-Fear/Landgrebe-Smith/p/book/978103294140 0''Why Humans Will Never Rule the World. Artificial Intelligence Without Fear''], Abingdon, UK: Routledge, 2025.</ref>

*2014 Fellow of the [[American College of Medical Informatics]] (FACMI)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.buffalo.edu/news/releases/2014/12/004.html|title=UB's Barry Smith named Fellow of American College of Medical Informatics|website=www.buffalo.edu}}</ref>
*2025 Fellow of the International Association for Ontology and Its Applications (FIAOA)<ref>{{Cite web|title=IAOA Fellows – IAOA |url=https://iaoa.org/index.php/organization/fellows}}</ref>

Leo Zaibert's ''The Theory and Practice of Ontology'' (2016)<ref>{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_raiDQAAQBAJ&q=dedicate+this+volume&pg=PA134 |title=The Theory and Practice of Ontology |editor=Leo Zaibert |publisher=Palgrave Macmillan |year=2016 |isbn=9781137552778 |page=1 }}</ref> and Gloria Zúñiga y Postigo and Gerald J. Erion's ''Barry Smith an sich'' (2017)<ref>''Cosmos + Taxis. Studies in Emergent Order and Organization'', 4 (4), June 2017. [https://cosmosandtaxis.files.wordpress.com/2017/06/ct_vol4_iss4.pdf]</ref> are [[Festschrift]]s containing studies of Smith's work by colleagues and students.
